highest_information_question: Can sovereign bond supply be represented more truthfully as expectation-adjusted private/free-float duration equivalents by maturity and marginal buyer, rather than scalar balance-sheet or QT dollars?

fresh_research.topic: Cross-central-bank evidence supports a duration-equivalent/free-float model rather than scalar QE/QT dollars
fresh_research.label: DURATION-SUPPLY MODEL / MATERIAL METHOD STRENGTHENING
observed_facts: Federal Reserve research measures SOMA holdings in ten-year equivalents (TYE), weighting par value by security duration relative to an on-the-run 10-year Treasury. The framework explicitly magnifies the economic importance of longer maturities and links the Fed portfolio's maturity composition to duration removed from private investors.

Federal Reserve research on the projected SOMA portfolio shows that term-premium effects evolve as the portfolio ages even without a simple one-for-one change in notional balance-sheet size. The relevant state is duration exposure removed from the private market, not dollars of securities alone.

ECB analysis of the APP models the term-premium channel through the current and expected future 'free float of duration risk' in private hands. It states that longer maturities have larger term-premium effects and that reinvestment can keep duration extracted even after net purchases stop, while portfolio ageing gradually returns duration risk to the market.

Bank of England July 2026 analysis estimates cumulative QT raised 10-year gilt yields by roughly 20-30 bp, but judges the much larger increase in term premia since 2022 was also driven by global policy uncertainty, high sovereign issuance and structurally weaker domestic long-gilt demand. The Bank explicitly treats the estimate as uncertain and regime-dependent.

The Bank of England July 2026 Market Participants Survey expected a median £50B APF reduction for Oct.2026-Sep.2027 and, among respondents expecting active sales, an average 15.6% long-maturity (>20y) sales weight. The September decision set an average £46B annual rundown but retained £120B of the longest gilts for banknote backing, set annual active sales at £20B, and paused APF auctions while implementation with the DMO is reviewed. Thus the aggregate pace change was modest relative to survey expectations, while the long-end composition/path changed much more substantially.

Federal Reserve 2024 work shows the marginal private buyer of Treasuries released by QT changes across regimes: households/dealers/foreign hedge funds featured in 2017-19, whereas households, dealers, insurers and the rest of the world were more important in the post-2022 episode. The paper states that the identity of the marginal buyer has implications for yield volatility.
fresh_research.inference: A more causally faithful sovereign-duration state variable is expectation-adjusted NET MARKET-FACING DURATION EQUIVALENTS by maturity bucket, combined with the balance-sheet elasticity of the marginal absorber. Notional QE/QT dollars are insufficient because securities with different maturities remove/release different amounts of duration risk, portfolio ageing changes duration without requiring the same notional change, reinvestment changes the expected future free float, and the same supply can clear at different yields depending on who must absorb it and their constraints.
fresh_research.causal_chain: fiscal issuance + central-bank purchases/retention/reinvestment/runoff/sales + debt-manager buybacks -> expected private free-float duration by maturity changes -> preferred-habitat/marginal buyers must absorb more or less duration -> dealer/arbitrage/intermediary capacity and structural pension/insurance/foreign demand determine price elasticity -> term premium/curve reprice -> mortgage/corporate discount rates and relative asset values change
fresh_research.matched_control: The September 2026 BoE case is consistent with a maturity-composition surprise mattering more than the small aggregate-pace surprise: the July survey already centered the next annual APF reduction near £50B, while the September plan averaged £46B but materially changed the long-end path and implementation. This remains a mechanism-supporting control, not a clean calibrated elasticity estimate, because simultaneous Bank Rate, energy and global-bond news affected yields.
negative_findings: Do not translate aggregate QE/QT dollars into a universal basis-point yield effect.
Do not assume unchanged balance-sheet notional means unchanged duration extraction; maturity ageing and reinvestment can change ten-year-equivalent exposure.
Do not assume active sales universally have a larger effect than passive runoff; credible studies disagree across designs and regimes.
Do not infer a trade from supply mechanics without measuring the pre-event expected path, policy-rate surprise, fiscal issuance, market depth and marginal buyer capacity.
Keep reserve-liquidity/funding-scarcity channels separate from the duration/term-premium channel; both can move financial conditions through different mechanisms.

learning_candidate.claim: For sovereign bond markets, model expectation-adjusted private/free-float duration equivalents by maturity and marginal-buyer risk-bearing capacity rather than scalar QE/QT or balance-sheet dollars. Notional size, duration composition, portfolio ageing, reinvestment/runoff, fiscal replacement issuance and buyer identity are distinct causal variables.
learning_candidate.promotion_note: Evidence is now cross-validated across Fed, ECB and BoE frameworks plus a Fed marginal-buyer study. Preserve uncertainty about effect size and active-versus-passive ranking; promote to the learning ledger only with a safe append path rather than rewriting/truncating the existing JSONL.

fresh_research.decision_support: Research-model upgrade only. No sovereign-duration BUY/SHORT clears the evidence bar from this mechanism alone.

fresh_research.topic: China rate hold is expectation-aligned and does not resolve weak-credit-demand transmission
fresh_research.label: MACRO EVENT CONTROL / WAIT
observed_facts: Reuters reported on September 20 that China kept the one-year LPR at 3.00% and the five-year LPR at 3.50% for a 16th consecutive month; all 21 analysts in its survey expected no change.
The same reporting describes weak credit demand from property and local-government sectors and constrained room for broad rate easing while major global central banks are tightening.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet in New York on September 20 on AI, trade and critical minerals ahead of the Trump-Xi summit; no agreement outcome was available at this cutoff.
fresh_research.inference: The fully expected LPR hold contains little clean policy surprise. China's current transmission problem should not be reduced to the administered price of credit alone: weak borrower balance sheets/credit demand and external yield constraints can limit the effect of small rate changes. The U.S.-China meeting remains future information, so sector winners should not be assigned from agenda headlines.
fresh_research.decision_support: WAIT / NO EDGE from the LPR headline or pre-meeting agenda alone.
